newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures finish firmer, all eyes on November.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures finish firmer, all eyes on November.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled a touch firmer in thin volume as many clung to the sidelines to watch the November contract expiry Friday because of its high open interest, traders said.
At the end of trade Tuesday, November's open interest was 4,509 lots. The spot contract gained 2.65 cents Wednesday to close at 111.95 cents a lb.
The November to most-active January spread has ballooned, to more than a 13-cent premium, up some 3 cents Wednesday.

"The market is waiting for this November delivery to resolve itself. The November contract only traded 78 contracts yesterday so whoever is in there is playing a game of chicken to wait the other one out," a broker said.
"It definitely has a dampening effect on the market because there is a taker out there who has that much orange juice on their hands without a home for it," the broker added.
The November premium reflected short-term tightness, but orange juice processing was due to start cranking-up which would lower prices.
This trend was reflected in the much lower most-active January contract which went out just 0.30 cent firmer at 98.75 cents per pound.
-- Huw Jones, New York Commodities 212-859-1646 REUTER
